info.title: AutoCRM API
info.description: Autotherm project lifecycle system. Money is integer minor units with an explicit currency; quantities are decimal strings. PATCH: omit a field to keep it, send null to clear it.

200.description: Signed in. Web clients also receive the httpOnly `autocrm_session` cookie.
Own preferences; defaults when never saved

204.description: Password reset; the user must change it at next login

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Matches name, tax number, e-mail, city — and phone in any
+36/06/0036 spacing variant.

parameters.name: role
parameters.description:
V2.6: `customer` or `supplier`. A partner with no role set counts as a customer,
so the picker never hides someone; `both` matches either filter.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort key, `-` prefix for descending: name, created_at.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description: Stage key.

parameters.name: open
parameters.description: Only leads not in a terminal stage.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort key, `-` prefix for descending: created_at, title.

200.description: Manual stage targets with note requirements; `won` is listed with `manual: false`

requestBody.description: `partner_id` may be omitted when the lead has one; `title` defaults to the lead's.

post.summary:
Send the quotation letter for a lead: hero band on top, the lead's quotation PDF
attached, from the staff member as themselves. Writing to a stranger's money needs a
person behind it, so this is `SendEmail` (office), not an automatic trigger.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches number, title, partner, VIN, and plate ignoring spaces and dashes.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description: Stage key.

parameters.name: open
parameters.description: Only orders not in a terminal stage.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
Sort key, `-` prefix for descending: created_at, due_date, total, number,
stage_entered_at (when the order entered its current stage).

200.description: Manual stage targets with note and gate requirements

get.summary:
Imported MiniCRM activity (V1.3). Read-only, and empty for orders created in AutoCRM:
this is history, not a task list.

put.summary:
Replaces the build spec. The form comes from the order's project type, never from the
request: a cooling order cannot be given a heating spec by sending one.

parameters.name: plate
parameters.description: Full vehicle history across orders, by plate.

post.summary: V2.4: a quotation PDF hangs off the lead it was sent for.

get.summary: V2.4: documents of a lead — the quotation, before any order exists.

The first cross-order document query in the system (V2.5). Without it a certificate is
reachable only through the one job it happened to be filed under.

parameters.name: expiring_before
parameters.description:
Certificates whose validity ends on or before this date. The question this query
exists for: "which ATP certificates expire next quarter".

patch.summary: Validity and vehicle on an existing document (V2.5, V2.1). The bytes never change.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description: Defaults to open orders only; pass `all=true` to include finished ones.

get.summary:
Everyone on the list, unsubscribed included: the office sees who opted out, because a
deleted address would silently resubscribe on the next import.

post.summary:
Website signup: `POST` with the address and `X-Newsletter-Key`. Resubscribing clears
an earlier unsubscribe — coming back is saying yes again.

403.description: Missing or wrong key, or signup is off

parameters.name: token
parameters.description:
The per-address token from an earlier mail. The page without a token asks for the
address instead — a BCC blast cannot carry personal links.

parameters.name: partner_id
parameters.description: Includes mail about the partner's orders and leads.

parameters.name: attention
parameters.description: Only failed and needs-review mail.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text over subject and recipient.

requestBody.description: Subject/body override the template. Unresolved variables are rejected.

202.description: Re-queued. Only failed or needs-review mail.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: month (default) | partner | project_type

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Defaults to 365 days before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Defaults to today.

get.summary:
Daily workshop load: placed, completed and in-workshop cars per business-tz day.
Ranges cap at 62 days — this feeds bar charts, not history exports.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Defaults to 6 days before `to` (one week).

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Defaults to today.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Defaults to 365 days before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Defaults to today.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: Defaults to EUR.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
At least 2 characters; shorter input returns empty groups rather than an error,
so the UI can query on every keystroke without special-casing.

get.summary:
The caller's open tasks: assigned to them or created by them, most urgent first.
This is what the dashboard widget reads.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: "failed" (default) or "pending"

post.summary: Runs a periodic job now instead of waiting for the scheduler ("send the nudges now").

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: `nudge_blockers` or `stalled_orders`

post.summary:
Send one test mail through the saved transport, or through an unsaved
candidate (validated first, never persisted). Always 200: delivery failure
is a diagnostic result, not a request error. Bypasses the queue like the
`email-test` CLI; in dry_run mode nothing leaves the machine.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Plate (ignoring spaces, dashes and case), VIN, make, model or notes.

post.summary: One job can cover several identical vans, each with its own MEO photos and certificate.
Issue an invoice for an order and report it to NAV.

409.description: An invoice is already in flight or live for this order

post.summary: Storno an issued invoice. The answer is the storno document, being reported.

422.description: Only an issued invoice can be stornoed

post.summary: Technically annul a data report. Admin only.

get.summary: The invoice's modification chain, straight from NAV.

post.summary: Render a proforma (díjbekérő) for an order.
post.description:
Nothing is reported to NAV, no invoice status changes, and no invoice needs to exist:
a proforma is a request for payment, and usable from the day the order is priced.

unit_price.description: Minor units in the order's currency. May be negative for discount lines.

email_redirect_to.description: Set during staging or the parallel run: all mail goes to this one address.

code.description: One of NAV's codes; `ERRATIC_DATA` is the usual one.

reason.description: Why. NAV stores it and shows it in the Online Számla portal.

mode.description:
"attached" or "link", filled in when the email is sent. "embedded" means the file
travels as an inline image under `content_id`, referenced from the HTML as
`cid:…` rather than listed as an attachment.

content_id.description: Content-ID without brackets (`doc-42`); only set together with mode "embedded".

is_overdue.description:
Past due date and still open, measured against the caller's business day
(not UTC midnight — the whole point of this flag).

BlockerBody.description: Create requires `what`. On PATCH every field is optional; `null` clears.

share_of_waiting.description: Fraction (0–1) of all blocker waiting time in the period.

waiting_days.description: Sum of (resolved or now − created) across blockers, in days.

ChainStep.description:
One document in the invoice's chain at NAV.

The sidecar speaks NAV's camelCase; this API does not. Restating the four fields the
screen uses keeps the contract in one shape rather than leaving a camelCase island in
the middle of it.

original_invoice_number.description: The document this one modifies, on a storno or a correction.

suggestions.description:
Suggested verdict per check-in damage: same zone + same type as a
check-out damage reads as pre-existing, anything else as new. The
inspector still confirms or dismisses each one.

body_markdown.description:
The body is Markdown: rendered to HTML for sending, kept as written for the text
part and the inbox. Templates stay plain text — Markdown and `{{variables}}` mix
badly when values contain asterisks, so a template plus this flag is refused.

hero.description:
Optional shout across the top of the HTML part (the quotation letter's band).
The text part never carries it.

embed_document_ids.description:
Documents shown inline: write `![alt](doc:ID)` in Markdown and pick the file here.
Sent as inline parts under `cid:doc-ID`, never as download links.

ContactBody.description: Create requires `name`. On PATCH every field is optional; `null` clears.

client_key.description:
Optional idempotency key (1..100 chars), e.g. the phone's local draft UUID.
A repeat create with the same key returns the inspection it already created
(200) instead of a second row or `checkout_open`. Reusing a key for a
different order or kind answers 409 `duplicate`.

tax_number.description: Hungarian tax numbers are normalised to `12345678-1-23`.

role.description:
`customer` | `supplier` | `both`. Omitted means unclassified, which the pickers
treat as a customer.

spec_form.description:
`heating` | `cooling` | omitted. Decides which build-spec section the order form
shows for this type; omitted means the type has no build spec.

key.description: Permanent; lowercase letters, digits and underscores.

existing.description:
True when this plate or VIN already existed and the stored vehicle was reused
rather than duplicated. The screen shows it as "this van has been here before",
which for a warranty job is the most useful thing the system can say.

order_id.description:
Exactly one of `order_id` and `lead_id` is set (V2.4): a quotation belongs to the
lead it was sent for, and had nowhere to live before this.

vehicle_id.description: Which vehicle on a multi-vehicle order this covers (V2.1). Usually null.

issuer.description: V2.5: an ATP certificate is issued by somebody and expires.
Who issued it — the ATP inspection body, the designer, the supplier.

vehicle_id.description: Which vehicle on a multi-vehicle order this covers.

bcc.description: A newsletter blast's recipients. Everyone else's rows leave this empty.

EmailSummary.description: List view: everything except the bodies.

ok.description: False means the mail did not go out; `detail` says why.

EmailTransportBody.description:
Email transport overrides. Every field is optional: absent keeps the stored
value, explicit null returns it to "inherit from the environment".
`mode: null` clears the whole transport back to environment behaviour.
`smtp_password`: absent keeps, null clears, a value replaces. Blank
strings are treated as absent everywhere (never a destructive surprise).

ErrorBody.description: The body of every non-2xx response.

ErrorCode.description: Every machine code `error.code` can carry. `x-error-catalog` gives each one's HTTP status, whether a retry can succeed, and the user-facing text.

message.description: Human-readable detail. For `validation` it names the field and the reason.

content_hash.description: Hex-encoded sha256 of the original file.

thumb_url.description: Presigned, expires after one hour; null until the thumbnail is generated.
Presigned, expires after one hour; null until generated.

number.description: The number NAV knows this document by.

original_invoice_id.description: The invoice this one cancels. Set exactly on a storno.

net_amount.description: Minor units (fillér / eurocent). Negative on a storno: it is the reversal.

nav_transaction_id.description: NAV's handle for the submission. Worth quoting in any support question.

nav_status.description: NAV's own per-invoice status: `DONE` when stored, `ABORTED` when rejected.

nav_error_code.description: NAV's fault code on a rejection, e.g. `INVOICE_NUMBER_ALREADY_EXISTS`.

nav_messages.description: Everything NAV said, including warnings on an accepted invoice.

document_id.description: The stored PDF, once there is one.

document_filename.description:
Filename of the stored PDF, when there is one. Download it through
`GET /documents/{id}/download` like any other document.

InvoiceDetail.description: An invoice with everything the screen shows about it.

InvoiceStatus.description:
Where an invoice is in its life.

`Submitting` is a real state, not a placeholder: NAV validates asynchronously, so there
is a period in which the report has been sent and no verdict exists. `Rejected` is
terminal for that document — the number is spent, and a corrected invoice is a new one.

IssueRequest.description:
What the caller may decide when issuing an invoice. Everything is optional: with an
order that already carries its line items, "issue the invoice" is a confirmation, not a
form.

vat_rate.description: The fraction, not the percentage: 0.27 is 27%. Defaults to `NAV_DEFAULT_VAT_RATE`.

issue_date.description: Defaults to today in the business timezone.

delivery_date.description: Fulfilment date. Defaults to the issue date.

payment_date.description: Defaults to the issue date plus `NAV_PAYMENT_DAYS`.

send_email.description: Send the customer the invoice once NAV has stored it.

unit_price.description: Minor units (fillér / eurocent). May be negative for discount lines.

line_total_minor.description: Backend-computed: round(quantity × unit_price), half away from zero.

is_overdue.description:
Past due date and still open, measured against the caller's business day
(not UTC midnight — the whole point of this flag).

items.description:
One document in the invoice's chain at NAV.

The sidecar speaks NAV's camelCase; this API does not. Restating the four fields the
screen uses keeps the contract in one shape rather than leaving a camelCase island in
the middle of it.

original_invoice_number.description: The document this one modifies, on a storno or a correction.

order_id.description:
Exactly one of `order_id` and `lead_id` is set (V2.4): a quotation belongs to the
lead it was sent for, and had nowhere to live before this.

vehicle_id.description: Which vehicle on a multi-vehicle order this covers (V2.1). Usually null.

issuer.description: V2.5: an ATP certificate is issued by somebody and expires.

items.description: List view: everything except the bodies.

thumb_url.description: Presigned, expires after one hour; null until the thumbnail is generated.

number.description: The number NAV knows this document by.

original_invoice_id.description: The invoice this one cancels. Set exactly on a storno.

net_amount.description: Minor units (fillér / eurocent). Negative on a storno: it is the reversal.

nav_transaction_id.description: NAV's handle for the submission. Worth quoting in any support question.

nav_status.description: NAV's own per-invoice status: `DONE` when stored, `ABORTED` when rejected.

nav_error_code.description: NAV's fault code on a rejection, e.g. `INVOICE_NUMBER_ALREADY_EXISTS`.

nav_messages.description: Everything NAV said, including warnings on an accepted invoice.

document_id.description: The stored PDF, once there is one.

line_total_minor.description: Backend-computed: round(quantity × unit_price), half away from zero.

minicrm_id.description: Provenance: the MiniCRM to-do this came from.

author_name.description: The MiniCRM user's name as text — those accounts do not exist in AutoCRM.

role.description:
V2.6: 'customer' | 'supplier' | 'both'. Null means not yet classified and is
treated as a customer by the pickers — the paint shop turning up in the customer
list is a nuisance, a customer missing from it is a bug.

document_id.description: The rendered PDF. Always present: a proforma is its document.

spec_form.description:
Which build-spec section the order form shows for this type: `heating`,
`cooling`, or null for work that has no build spec (repairs). Configuration, so
the office can retype a category without a deploy.

items.description:
One manual stage target, with everything the UI needs to present it
without reimplementing the transition rules: whether a hand move there is
allowed at all, whether it needs a note, and whether its image gates pass.
Computed from the same `check_transition` the move itself goes through.

manual.description: False for targets unreachable by a manual move (lead `won`: conversion only).

requires_note.description: True when the move needs a note (backward or reopen).

gates_met.description: False when an image gate between current and target is unmet.

plate_norm.description: Plate with spaces, dashes and case removed. Generated column; search matches on it.

job_id.description: Null when an identical job was already queued.

quoted_value_minor.description:
V2.3: what we quoted, in minor units. Not a `quotes` table with versions — at 60
leads a month that is more machinery than the business justifies. Changes are
written to audit_log, so a revised price still leaves a trail.

LeadBody.description: Create requires `title`. On PATCH every field is optional; `null` clears.

quoted_value_minor.description: V2.3: the quoted price in minor units (fillér / eurocent).

orders.description:
V2.7: every order this enquiry became. Three identical Sprinters from one enquiry
are three orders, and all three point back here.

documents.description: V2.4: the quotation and anything else filed against the enquiry itself.

client.description: `web` (default) sets the session cookie; `mobile` returns a bearer token.

token.description: Mobile clients only: send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

NavMessage.description: One finding, as the sidecar flattens NAV's technical and business messages.

code.description: NAV's own fault code, where there is one.

NewsletterRequest.description:
A newsletter blast: one row, everyone in BCC, nobody sees the list.

Bodies are literal — a blast has no single partner or lead, so `{{variables}}` have
nothing to resolve against, and any braces found refuse the send loudly rather than
mailing `{{MISSING:…}}` to hundreds of people. Unsubscribed and globally suppressed
addresses never make the BCC list.

hero.description: Optional shout across the top (the quotation-style band for offer blasts).

attachment_document_ids.description:
Any company documents: a blast has no order or lead, so ownership is not
checked — the endpoint is office-only, and the list is company mail.

embed_document_ids.description: Documents shown inline via `![alt](doc:ID)`, sent as `cid:doc-ID` parts.

NewsletterSent.description:
One row, everyone in BCC. The answer says how many addresses made the list, so the
office knows what "sent" meant.

related_order_id.description:
V2.2: the job this one repairs or repeats. Warranty and rework work is otherwise
unlinkable to the job it fixes, and nobody reconstructs that afterwards.

relation.description: 'warranty' | 'rework' | 'repeat'. Set together with related_order_id or not at all.

mileage_in.description: Intake slip (átvételi lap): odometer at takeover. Leaving `intake` requires it.

intake_condition.description: Intake slip: visible condition notes at takeover.

fuel_level.description: Intake slip: fuel level at takeover (`E` | `1/4` | `1/2` | `3/4` | `F`).

key_count.description: Intake slip: how many keys were handed over.

valuables_declared.description:
Intake slip: whether the valuables question was answered at all, and how.
`None` means nobody asked; `Some(false)` means the vehicle was empty.

valuables.description: Intake slip: what was left in the vehicle, when [`Self::valuables_declared`] is true.

valuation_date.description: Defaults to today. Reports normalise the order's value at this date's MNB rate.

related_order_id.description: V2.2: the job this one repairs or repeats. Set with `relation` or not at all.

mileage_in.description: Intake slip: odometer at takeover (km). Leaving `intake` requires it.

intake_condition.description: Intake slip: visible condition notes at takeover.

fuel_level.description: Intake slip: fuel gauge at takeover — `E`, `1/4`, `1/2`, `3/4` or `F`.

key_count.description: Intake slip: how many keys were handed over.

valuables_declared.description:
Intake slip: whether anyone answered the valuables question. Absent means nobody
did, which is not the same as `false` — "we never asked" is not a defence.

valuables.description:
Intake slip: what was left in the vehicle. Only meaningful with
`valuables_declared = true`, and rejected without it.

oneOf.description:
The build specification, when the chosen project type asks for one. Written in the
same transaction as the order so a failed second request cannot leave a build with
no spec.
V2.2: the job this one repairs or repeats, resolved for display.

vehicles.description:
V2.1: the vans this job covers. Usually one; three identical Sprinters from one
enquiry is the case the join table exists for.

oneOf.description: The build specification, when the project type asks for one.

image_counts.description: Image count per category; categories without images are absent.

OrderHit.description: One order hit: enough to recognise the job (number + plate + stage) and link to it.

minicrm_id.description: Provenance: the MiniCRM to-do this came from.

author_name.description: The MiniCRM user's name as text — those accounts do not exist in AutoCRM.

atp_class.description: ATP classification (FNA, FRC, …). Free text until the real list is confirmed.

sha256.description: Hex sha256 of the original file.

role.description:
V2.6: 'customer' | 'supplier' | 'both'. Null means not yet classified and is
treated as a customer by the pickers — the paint shop turning up in the customer
list is a nuisance, a customer missing from it is a bug.

leads.description:
Every enquiry from this partner, quoted or not. Without it, someone opening a
partner cannot see they were quoted eight months ago and never followed up.

partner_id.description: Changing partner without naming `contact_id` clears the contact.

oneOf.description: Rejected with `422 currency_locked` while the order has line items.

spec_form.description: Absent keeps the current form; explicit null removes the build-spec section.

PresignedRequest.description: A request the client must perform exactly as described: every header listed is signed.

headers.description: `[name, value]` pairs; every one must be sent unchanged.

recipient_suppressed.description: Manual mail may still go to a suppressed address; the UI should warn.

document_id.description: The rendered PDF. Always present: a proforma is its document.

email_id.description: Queued letter, when one was asked for and the customer has an address.

ProformaCreated.description: A rendered proforma and the document it was stored as.

note.description: Printed under the totals, e.g. payment instructions.

spec_form.description:
Which build-spec section the order form shows for this type: `heating`,
`cooling`, or null for work that has no build spec (repairs). Configuration, so
the office can retype a category without a deploy.

QuotationRequest.description:
A quotation letter for a lead: the one letter that shouts. Hero band on top, the
lead's quotation PDF attached, sent by the staff member as themselves.

The price and validity lines appear when the lead carries them; the PDF is
authoritative either way, so a lead without a quoted price still sends. Anything the
office writes by hand goes through `{{variable}}` rendering first, then Markdown when
asked — the same pipeline as a manual letter.

hero.description: The hero band. Defaults to the shout; the office can tone it down per send.

minicrm_id.description: The MiniCRM id this row came from; null for records created in AutoCRM.

raw_import.description:
The complete source record as MiniCRM returned it. Null for records created in
AutoCRM — the screen shows nothing rather than an empty panel.

SessionUser.description: The signed-in user as clients see it. Login and `/auth/me` return the same shape.

must_change_password.description:
While true, every endpoint except `/auth/me`, `/auth/password` and `/auth/logout`
answers `422 password_change_required`.

automatic_email_enabled.description: The kill switch for automatic email.

email.description: Email transport overrides; absent keeps everything stored.

document_id.description: Finger-drawn PNG uploaded as an `other` document of the same order.

SpecBody.description:
The build spec as the form sends it. `form` is not taken on trust: it must match what
the order's project type asks for, or the row would mean something the office did not
choose.

note.description: Required for backward moves and reopening a terminal stage.

visits.description: Stage visits that started in the period.

avg_days.description: Statistics over finished visits only; open visits would understate them.

issue_date.description: Defaults to today in the business timezone.

median_lead_days.description: First stage entry → completion, in days.

TransitionOption.description:
One manual stage target, with everything the UI needs to present it
without reimplementing the transition rules: whether a hand move there is
allowed at all, whether it needs a note, and whether its image gates pass.
Computed from the same `check_transition` the move itself goes through.

manual.description: False for targets unreachable by a manual move (lead `won`: conversion only).

requires_note.description: True when the move needs a note (backward or reopen).

gates_met.description: False when an image gate between current and target is unmet.

Unsubscribed.description:
Unsubscribe from a link or a typed address. Always answers 200 with whether anything
changed: a link clicked twice is not an error, and guessing addresses learns nothing.

sha256.description: Hex sha256 of the file, computed by the client before upload.

oneOf.description:
Perform `upload` exactly as given (all headers are signed), then POST the ticket to
/api/uploads/complete.
This exact file is already attached to the order. Nothing to upload.

plate_norm.description: Plate with spaces, dashes and case removed. Generated column; search matches on it.

orders.description: Every job this van has been through, newest first.

normalized_huf_minor.description: Everything normalised to HUF at each order's valuation-date MNB rate.

missing_fx.description: Orders excluded from the normalised sum because no rate was available.

completed.description: Orders that reached a terminal stage that day.

in_workshop.description: Orders sitting in the workshop that day (placed, not yet completed).
